The NRI and FEMA lenses add long-record evidence.\n\n## D10 — Two scores: long-term exposure and near-term risk\n\n- **Decision:**\n  - **Exposure** (for investment): long-term, 5 hazard families, mean-based.\n  - **Near-term risk** (for alerts): next 7 days, forecast + NWS alerts, max-based.\n- **Why:** Investment cares about chronic exposure across hazards. Operations care about the worst hazard this week. Mixing the two would blur both.\n\n## D11 — Fixed-anchor normalization, not min-max\n\n- **Decision:** Each indicator maps to 0–100 through documented anchors (e.g. 25 snow days/yr = 100), capped.\n- **Why:** A hub's score doesn't move when other hubs are added or removed, so a score change always means a data change. That is what makes alerts meaningful.\n- **Rejected:** Min-max or rank scaling across the roster.\n\n## D12 — Overall exposure = equal-weight mean of families\n\n- **Decision:** Overall = mean of winter, hurricane, flood, severe storm and heat (user decision). Weights can be overridden per question.\n- **Why:** It's the most neutral default without the company's own loss data.\n- **Trade-off:** A hub with one extreme hazard (Miami/hurricane) is diluted. To compensate, answers always show each hub's top hazard, and hazard-specific questions rank by family.\n- **Rejected:** A \"mean + worst hazard\" blend, and judgment-based disruption weights.\n\n## D13 — Stat thresholds in config, always printed\n\n- **Decision:** \"Snowfall day\" means ≥ 0.25 cm (the NWS \"measurable\" 0.1 in). Every stat answer also shows a sensitivity row.\n- **Why:** For Denver 2025 the threshold swings the answer from 2.7% to 12.1%:\n\n  | Threshold | Days | % of 2025 |\n  |---|---|---|\n  | Any snow > 0 | 44 | 12.1% |\n  | ≥ 0.25 cm (measurable) | 31 | 8.5% |\n  | ≥ 1 cm | 18 | 4.9% |\n  | ≥ 2.5 cm (1 in) | 10 | 2.7% |\n\n  Reanalysis also differs from the station (26 measurable-snow days at Denver airport).\n\n## D14 — SQLite + committed seed snapshot\n\n- **Decision:** One SQLite file (WAL mode, stdlib `sqlite3`, no ORM). Real API responses are recorded once into `data/seed/` and used for tests, offline eval and first-run seeding.\n- **Why:**\n  - The data is tiny (~55k daily rows).\n  - It needs date-range queries and atomic writes for scores, alerts and conversations.\n  - Zero ops, and easy to inspect.\n  - With the seed, a fresh install works without a paced 15-minute download.\n- **Rejected:**\n  - Postgres: no concurrency need. It's the migration path for multi-instance.\n  - JSON files: no range queries or transactions.\n  - DuckDB: built for analytics, not small transactional writes.\n\n## D15 — One run script; Docker optional; no cloud deploy yet\n\n- **Decision:** `uv run python scripts/run.py` starts FastAPI (:8000) and Streamlit (:8501) together and stops both together. The Dockerfile runs the same script. There is no Makefile. The cloud host will be chosen later (user decision).\n- **Why:** One obvious way to run the app, with or without Docker. Env-only config keeps it deployable to any container host later.\n\n## D16 — Eval: offline by default, `--live` for the real LLM\n\n- **Decision:** 22 cases built around the four example questions, including follow-ups and guardrails.\n  - **Offline:** feeds each case's expected plan to the executor and uses the template explainer on seed data. No keys, no network.\n  - **`--live`:** runs the real planner and explainer on the same seed data.\n- **Why:** Offline checks the deterministic core and the answer contract on every run. Live measures plan accuracy and grounding. Pinning the data keeps expected numbers stable.\n\n## D17 — Pragmatic TDD for core logic\n\n- **Decision:** Core logic (scoring, stats, plan validation, grounding check, executor, assembler, alert diff) is written test-first, with hand-computed fixtures. I/O glue is tested alongside, with every external call mocked.\n- **Why:** The numbers are the product, so they get the strongest guarantees. Test-first on glue code would add little.\n\n## D18 — Identity-lite auth\n\n- **Decision:** An allow-listed email gets a signed bearer token with an `analyst` or `admin` role. Ingest and alert runs are admin-only. Built after the core works.\n- **Why:** This is the light auth the brief asks for.\n- **Limitation (documented):** There is no password or magic link. This is not production authentication.\n\n## D19 — Hub roster is an assumption\n\n- **Decision:** 15 hubs, each placed at its metro's main airport logistics zone, with the county looked up once via the FCC Area API:\n  - Midwest (US Census definition): Chicago, Indianapolis, Columbus, Detroit, Minneapolis–St Paul, Kansas City, St. Louis\n  - Named in the brief: Denver, Dallas, Houston, Miami\n  - Others: Atlanta, Memphis, Newark, Los Angeles\n- **Why:** The brief gives no facility list. The roster covers the example questions, and Los Angeles serves as a low-exposure control. It lives in `config/hubs.yaml` and can be replaced.\n"
}

- **FEMA's combined loss-rate percentile counts farm losses.** Miami shows a 91st-percentile cold-wave risk because of crop freezes, which is why the ranking uses building losses only.
- **The snow threshold decides the Denver answer.** Last year ranges from 2.7% to 12.1% of days depending on what counts as a snowfall day, so every statistic answer will state its threshold and show the alternatives.

# CLAUDE.md

Weather Risk Intelligence Agent: a chat agent that ranks, compares and explains the weather-disruption exposure of US logistics hubs.

- Task: [docs/TASK.md](docs/TASK.md)
- Plan: [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md)
- Decisions: [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md)

## Design principles

- **Numbers come from code.** Scores, ranks and percentages come from deterministic Python. The LLM turns questions into a schema-validated query plan and explains the computed results. This keeps every number auditable, which is the point of the scoring requirement.
- **Validate all LLM output** against Pydantic/JSON schemas. On failure, retry once with the error included, then return a clear error.
- **Real data only.** Weather data comes only from real API responses. When a source fails or has gaps, say so in the answer, because analysts need to know how far to trust a ranking.
- **Every answer states** its assumptions, its uncertainty, its data sources and its time window.
- **Build only what the assignment asks**, with no extra abstractions. If time runs short, cut bonuses before tests or docs.

## Development rules

- **Pragmatic TDD for core logic** (scoring, stats, date resolution, plan validation, grounding check, executor, answer contract, alert diff):
  - Write a failing test first, then implement, then refactor.
  - Use small hand-computable fixtures. Work out expected values by hand; never copy them from the implementation's output.
- **I/O glue** (HTTP clients, API routes, LLM wrapper): write tests alongside the code. Mock every external call (respx, mocked LiteLLM).
- **Each milestone:** full suite green, then commit.
- **Config is the source of truth.** Thresholds, anchors, weights and bands live in `config/scoring.yaml`; hubs live in `config/hubs.yaml`. Don't hard-code them.
- **LLM:** go through LiteLLM only. Primary is Groq `openai/gpt-oss-20b` (strict JSON schema); Gemini is the fallback. Keep prompts compact, because Groq's free tier allows 8K tokens/min.
- **Running:**
  - `uv run python scripts/run.py` starts the API and Streamlit together.
  - Docker is optional; the image runs the same script.
  - There is no Makefile.
- **Docs:** short, clear Markdown.

The message is safe to show to analysts.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, source: str, message: str):\n        super().__init__(f\"{source}: {message}\")\n        self.source = source\n        self.message = message\n\n\ndef make_client(contact_email: str, timeout: float = 30.0) -> httpx.AsyncClient:\n    return httpx.AsyncClient(\n        timeout=timeout,\n        headers={\"User-Agent\": f\"(weather-risk-agent, {contact_email})\"},\n        follow_redirects=True,\n    )\n\n\nasync def get_json(\n    client: httpx.AsyncClient,\n    url: str,\n    *,\n    source: str,\n    params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,\n    retries: int = 2,\n    backoff_s: float = 1.0,\n) -> Any:\n    last_error = \"\"\n    for attempt in range(retries + 1):\n        try:\n            response = await client.get(url, params=params)\n        except httpx.TransportError as exc:\n            last_error = f\"network error: {exc.__class__.__name__}\"\n        else:\n            if response.status_code in RETRY_STATUSES:\n                last_error = f\"HTTP {response.status_code}\"\n                retry_after = response.headers.get(\"Retry-After\", \"\")\n                if retry_after.isdigit():\n                    backoff_s = max(backoff_s, min(float(retry_after), 30.0))\n            elif response.status_code >= 400:\n                raise SourceError(source, f\"HTTP {response.status_code}: {response.text[:200]}\")\n            else:\n                try:\n                    return response.json()\n                except ValueError as exc:\n                    raise SourceError(source, \"response was not valid JSON\") from exc\n        if attempt < retries:\n            await asyncio.sleep(backoff_s * 2**attempt)\n    raise SourceError(source, f\"failed after {retries + 1} attempts ({last_error})\")\n"
}

Requests longer than 2 weeks or with\nmore than 10 variables count as several API calls (see `call_weight`).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom datetime import date, timedelta\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport httpx\n\nfrom weather_risk.sources.http import get_json\n\nARCHIVE_URL = \"https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive\"\nFORECAST_URL = \"https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast\"\nARCHIVE_LAG_DAYS = 6\nATTRIBUTION = \"Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0), ERA5 reanalysis\"\n\n# Open-Meteo daily variable → our column, with the unit we require.\nDAILY_VARS = {\n    \"snowfall_sum\": (\"snowfall_cm\", \"cm\"),\n    \"precipitation_sum\": (\"precip_mm\", \"mm\"),\n    \"temperature_2m_max\": (\"tmax_c\", \"°C\"),\n    \"temperature_2m_min\": (\"tmin_c\", \"°C\"),\n    \"wind_gusts_10m_max\": (\"gust_kmh\", \"km/h\"),\n}\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass DailyRow:\n    date: date\n    snowfall_cm: float | None\n    precip_mm: float | None\n    tmax_c: float | None\n    tmin_c: float | None\n    gust_kmh: float | None\n\n\ndef archive_end(today: date) -> date:\n    \"\"\"Last day the archive reliably has data for (ERA5T lag).\"\"\"\n    return today - timedelta(days=ARCHIVE_LAG_DAYS)\n\n\ndef call_weight(n_days: int, n_vars: int = len(DAILY_VARS)) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Fractional API-call cost of one request (Open-Meteo pricing rule).\"\"\"\n    return max(1.0, n_days / 14) * max(1.0, n_vars / 10)\n\n\ndef _params(lat: float, lon: float) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    return {\"latitude\": lat, \"longitude\": lon, \"daily\": \",\".join(DAILY_VARS), \"timezone\": \"auto\"}\n\n\nasync def fetch_archive(client: httpx.AsyncClient, lat: float, lon: float, start: date, end: date) -> dict:\n    params = _params(lat, lon) | {\"start_date\": start.isoformat(), \"end_date\": end.isoformat()}\n    return await get_json(client, ARCHIVE_URL, source=\"open_meteo_archive\", params=params)\n\n\nasync def fetch_forecast(client: httpx.AsyncClient, lat: float, lon: float, days: int = 7) -> dict:\n    params = _params(lat, lon) | {\"forecast_days\": days}\n    return await get_json(client, FORECAST_URL, source=\"open_meteo_forecast\", params=params)\n\n\ndef parse_daily(payload: dict) -> list[DailyRow]:\n    \"\"\"Parse a daily payload. Rejects unexpected units instead of silently converting.\"\"\"\n    units = payload.get(\"daily_units\", {})\n    for api_name, (_, unit) in DAILY_VARS.items():\n        if units.get(api_name) != unit:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Open-Meteo returned {api_name} in {units.get(api_name)!r}, expected {unit!r}\")\n    daily = payload[\"daily\"]\n    columns = {col: daily[api_name] for api_name, (col, _) in DAILY_VARS.items()}\n    return [\n        DailyRow(date=date.fromisoformat(day), **{col: values[i] for col, values in columns.items()})\n        for i, day in enumerate(daily[\"time\"])\n    ]\n\n\ndef grid_cell(payload: dict) -> dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"The reanalysis grid cell the coordinates snapped to.\"\"\"\n    return {k: payload[k] for k in (\"latitude\", \"longitude\", \"elevation\")}\n"
}

Alert free text (description, instructions) is\ndropped on purpose so it can never reach the LLM prompt.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nimport httpx\n\nfrom weather_risk.sources.http import get_json\n\nALERTS_URL = \"https://api.weather.gov/alerts/active\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass NwsAlert:\n    event: str\n    severity: str\n    urgency: str\n    certainty: str\n    onset: str | None\n    expires: str | None\n\n\nasync def fetch_active_alerts(client: httpx.AsyncClient, lat: float, lon: float) -> dict:\n    return await get_json(client, ALERTS_URL, source=\"nws_alerts\", params={\"point\": f\"{lat:.4f},{lon:.4f}\"})\n\n\ndef parse_alerts(payload: dict) -> list[NwsAlert]:\n    alerts = []\n    for feature in payload.get(\"features\", []):\n        p = feature.get(\"properties\", {})\n        if p.get(\"status\") != \"Actual\" or p.get(\"messageType\") == \"Cancel\":\n            continue\n        alerts.append(\n            NwsAlert(\n                event=p.get(\"event\", \"Unknown\"),\n                severity=p.get(\"severity\") or \"Unknown\",\n                urgency=p.get(\"urgency\") or \"Unknown\",\n                certainty=p.get(\"certainty\") or \"Unknown\",\n                onset=p.get(\"onset\"),\n                expires=p.get(\"expires\"),\n            )\n        )\n    return alerts\n"

We keep major disasters (DR) only and\nde-duplicate by disaster number; incident-type filtering happens in scoring.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom datetime import date\n\nimport httpx\n\nfrom weather_risk.sources.http import get_json\n\nURL = \"https://www.fema.gov/api/open/v2/DisasterDeclarationsSummaries\"\nFIELDS = \"disasterNumber,declarationType,declarationDate,incidentType,declarationTitle,fipsStateCode,fipsCountyCode\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Declaration:\n    disaster_number: int\n    incident_type: str\n    declaration_date: date\n    title: str\n\n\nasync def fetch_declarations(client: httpx.AsyncClient, county_fips: str, since: date) -> dict:\n    flt = (\n        f\"fipsStateCode eq '{county_fips[:2]}' and fipsCountyCode eq '{county_fips[2:]}' \"\n        f\"and declarationDate ge '{since.isoformat()}T00:00:00.000Z'\"\n    )\n    params = {\"$filter\": flt, \"$select\": FIELDS, \"$orderby\": \"declarationDate desc\", \"$top\": 1000}\n    return await get_json(client, URL, source=\"openfema\", params=params)\n\n\ndef parse_declarations(payload: dict) -> list[Declaration]:\n    \"\"\"Major-disaster (DR) declarations only, one per disaster number.\"\"\"\n    seen: dict[int, Declaration] = {}\n    for row in payload.get(\"DisasterDeclarationsSummaries\", []):\n        if row.get(\"declarationType\") != \"DR\":\n            continue\n        number = int(row[\"disasterNumber\"])\n        seen.setdefault(\n            number,\n            Declaration(\n                disaster_number=number,\n                incident_type=row[\"incidentType\"],\n                declaration_date=date.fromisoformat(row[\"declarationDate\"][:10]),\n                title=row.get(\"declarationTitle\", \"\"),\n            ),\n        )\n    return sorted(seen.values(), key=lambda d: d.declaration_date, reverse=True)\n"

    \"orderByFields\": \"OBJECTID\",\n            \"resultOffset\": offset,\n            \"resultRecordCount\": PAGE_SIZE,\n            \"f\": \"json\",\n        }\n        page = await Stay well under it when pulling years of history.\nOPEN_METEO_CALLS_PER_MIN = 400\n\n\n# -- apply: parsed payload → store (shared by live ingest and seed loading) ---------\n\ndef apply_archive(store: Store, hub: Hub, payload: dict) -> int:\n    rows = open_meteo.parse_daily(payload)\n    store.upsert_daily(hub.id, rows)\n    store.cache_put(f\"grid:{hub.id}\", \"open_meteo_archive\", open_meteo.grid_cell(payload))\n    return len(rows)\n\n\ndef apply_forecast(store: Store, hub: Hub, payload: dict, fetched_at: str | None = None) -> None:\n    rows = [asdict(r) for r in open_meteo.parse_daily(payload)]\n    store.cache_put(f\"forecast:{hub.id}\", \"open_meteo_forecast\", {\"rows\": rows}, fetched_at)\n\n\ndef apply_nws(store: Store, hub: Hub, payload: dict, fetched_at: str | None = None) -> None:\n    alerts = [asdict(a) for a in nws.parse_alerts(payload)]\n    store.cache_put(f\"nws:{hub.id}\", \"nws_alerts\", alerts, fetched_at)\n\n\ndef apply_declarations(store: Store, hub: Hub, payload: dict, fetched_at: str | None = None) -> None:\n    decls = [asdict(d) for d in openfema.parse_declarations(payload)]\n    store.cache_put(f\"openfema:{hub.id}\", \"openfema\", decls, fetched_at)\n\n\ndef apply_nri(store: Store, hubs: list[Hub], pages: list[dict], fetched_at: str | None = None) -> None:\n    version, n, by_fips = nri.county_percentiles(pages, [h.county_fips for h in hubs])\n    payload = {\n        \"version\": version,\n        \"n_counties\": n,\n        \"by_fips\": {f: {hz: asdict(v) for hz, v in hz_map.items()} for f, hz_map in by_fips.items()},\n    }\n    store.cache_put(\"nri\", \"fema_nri\", payload, fetched_at)\n\n\n# -- live refresh ------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _fresh(store: Store, key: str, ttl: timedelta) -> bool:\n    cached = store.cache_get(key)\n    if not cached:\n        return False\n    return datetime.now(UTC) - datetime.fromisoformat(cached[0]) < ttl\n\n\nasync def _guarded(store: Store, source: str, errors: list[str], coro) -> None:\n    try:\n        await coro\n        store.source_ok(source)\n    except (SourceError, ValueError, KeyError) as exc:\n        message = str(exc)\n        store.source_error(source, message)\n        errors.append(message)\n        log.warning(\"%s failed: %s\", source, message)\n\n\nasync def refresh_nri(store: Store, client: httpx.AsyncClient, hubs: list[Hub], force: bool) -> None:\n    if not force and _fresh(store, \"nri\", TTL[\"fema_nri\"]):\n        return\n    apply_nri(store, hubs, await nri.fetch_county_pages(client))\n\n\nasync def refresh_declarations(store: Store, client: httpx.AsyncClient, hub: Hub, since: date, force: bool) -> None:\n    if not force and _fresh(store, f\"openfema:{hub.id}\", TTL[\"openfema\"]):\n        return\n    apply_declarations(store, hub, await openfema.fetch_declarations(client, hub.county_fips, since))\n\n\nasync def refresh_archive(store: Store, client: httpx.AsyncClient, hub: Hub, start: date, end: date, pace: bool) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Fetch only dates not yet stored. History never changes, so it is never refetched.\"\"\"\n    have = store.daily_range(hub.id)\n    ranges = []\n    if have is None:\n        ranges.append((start, end))\n    else:\n        if have[0] > start:\n            ranges.append((start, have[0] - timedelta(days=1)))\n        if have[1] < end:\n            ranges.append((have[1] + timedelta(days=1), end))\n    fetched = 0\n    for a, b in ranges:\n        fetched += apply_archive(store, hub, await open_meteo.fetch_archive(client, hub.lat, hub.lon, a, b))\n        weight = open_meteo.call_weight((b - a).days + 1)\n        if pace and weight > 20:\n            await asyncio.sleep(weight * 60 / OPEN_METEO_CALLS_PER_MIN)\n    return fetched\n\n\nasync def refresh_near_term(store: Store, client: httpx.AsyncClient, hub: Hub, force: bool, errors: list[str]) -> None:\n    if force or not _fresh(store, f\"forecast:{hub.id}\", TTL[\"open_meteo_forecast\"]):\n        async def forecast():\n            apply_forecast(store, hub, await open_meteo.fetch_forecast(client, hub.lat, hub.lon))\n        await _guarded(store, \"open_meteo_forecast\", errors, forecast())\n    if force or not _fresh(store, f\"nws:{hub.id}\", TTL[\"nws_alerts\"]):\n        async def alerts():\n            apply_nws(store, hub, await nws.fetch_active_alerts(client, hub.lat, hub.lon))\n        await _guarded(store, \"nws_alerts\", errors, alerts())\n\n\nasync def run_ingest(\n    store: Store,\n    client: httpx.AsyncClient,\n    *,\n    hubs: list[Hub] | None = None,\n    today: date | None = None,\n    history: bool = True,\n    near_term: bool = True,\n    force: bool = False,\n    pace: bool = True,\n) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Refresh data and recompute snapshots. Returns error messages (empty = all sources OK).\"\"\"\n    hubs = list(hubs or load_hubs())\n    today = today or date.today()\n    cfg = load_scoring_config()\n    errors: list[str] = []\n    if history:\n        await _guarded(store, \"fema_nri\", errors, refresh_nri(store, client, list(load_hubs()), force))\n        since = cfg[\"declarations_since\"]\n        for hub in hubs:\n            await _guarded(store, \"openfema\", errors, refresh_declarations(store, client, hub, since, force))\n        start, end = cfg[\"climatology\"][\"start\"], open_meteo.archive_end(today)\n        for hub in hubs:\n            log.info(\"archive %s\", hub.id)\n            await _guarded(store, \"open_meteo_archive\", errors, refresh_archive(store, client, hub, start, end, pace))\n    if near_term:\n        for hub in hubs:\n            await refresh_near_term(store, client, hub, force, errors)\n    from weather_risk.scoring.snapshots import refresh_snapshots  # scoring depends on ingest output\n\n    refresh_snapshots(store, today=today)\n    return errors\n\n\n# -- seed snapshot (recorded real responses, see scripts/record_seed.py) -------\n\ndef read_gz(path: Path) -> Any:\n    with gzip.open(path, \"rt\") as f:\n        return json.load(f)\n\n\ndef write_gz(path: Path, payload: Any) -> None:\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    with gzip.open(path, \"wt\", compresslevel=9) as f:\n        json.dump(payload, f, separators=(\",\", \":\"))\n\n\ndef load_seed(store: Store, seed_dir: Path, today: date | None = None) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Load the recorded seed into the store. Freshness is the recording time, not now.\"\"\"\n    manifest = json.loads((seed_dir / \"manifest.json\").read_text())\n    at = manifest[\"recorded_at\"]\n    hubs = list(load_hubs())\n    apply_nri(store, hubs, read_gz(seed_dir / \"nri_pages.json.gz\"), at)\n    store.source_ok(\"fema_nri\", at)\n    for hub in hubs:\n        apply_archive(store, hub, read_gz(seed_dir / \"archive\" / f\"{hub.id}.json.gz\"))\n        apply_forecast(store, hub, read_gz(seed_dir / \"forecast\" / f\"{hub.id}.json.gz\"), at)\n        apply_nws(store, hub, read_gz(seed_dir / \"nws\" / f\"{hub.id}.json.gz\"), at)\n        apply_declarations(store, hub, read_gz(seed_dir / \"openfema\" / f\"{hub.id}.json.gz\"), at)\n    for source in (\"open_meteo_archive\", \"open_meteo_forecast\", \"nws_alerts\", \"openfema\"):\n        store.source_ok(source, at)\n    from weather_risk.scoring.snapshots import refresh_snapshots\n\n    refresh_snapshots(store, today=today or date.fromisoformat(manifest[\"today\"]))\n    return manifest\n\n\ndef ensure_data(store: Store, seed_dir: Path) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Seed an empty database so a fresh install works without the paced history pull.\"\"\"\n    if store.has_weather():\n        return False\n    load_seed(store, seed_dir)\n    return True\n\n\nasync def _main() -> None:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Refresh weather and hazard data.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--hub\", action=\"append\", help=\"hub id (repeatable); default: all\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--seed\", action=\"store_true\", help=\"load data/seed/ into the database and exit\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--no-history\", action=\"store_true\", help=\"skip archive/NRI/FEMA; refresh near-term only\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--force\", action=\"store_true\", help=\"ignore cache TTLs\")\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format=\"%(message)s\")\n\n    settings = get_settings()\n    store = Store(settings.db_path)\n    if args.seed:\n        manifest = load_seed(store, settings.seed_dir)\n        print(f\"Seed loaded (recorded {manifest['recorded_at']}).\")\n        return\n    by_id = {h.id: h for h in load_hubs()}\n    hubs = [by_id[h] for h in args.hub] if args.hub else list(by_id.values())\n    async with make_client(settings.contact_email) as client:\n        errors = await run_ingest(store, client, hubs=hubs, history=not args.no_history, force=args.force)\n    for hub in hubs:\n        rng = store.daily_range(hub.id)\n        print(f\"{hub.id:12} daily rows {rng[0]} → {rng[1]}\" if rng else f\"{hub.id:12} no daily rows\")\n    print(\"All sources OK.\" if not errors else f\"{len(errors)} source error(s):\\n  \" + \"\\n  \".join(errors))\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    asyncio.run(_main())\n"
}

Winter Storm Warning, Severe → 80 → band Severe; hurricane alert, Moderate → 50\n    alerts = [\n        {\"event\": \"Winter Storm Warning\", \"severity\": \"Severe\", \"urgency\": \"Expected\", \"certainty\": \"Likely\", \"onset\": None, \"expires\": \"2026-10-03T00:00:00-05:00\"},\n        {\"event\": \"Hurricane Watch\", \"severity\": \"Moderate\", \"urgency\": \"Future\", \"certainty\": \"Possible\", \"onset\": None, \"expires\": None},\n        {\"event\": \"Air Quality Alert\", \"severity\": \"Minor\", \"urgency\": \"Expected\", \"certainty\": \"Likely\", \"onset\": None, \"expires\": None},\n    ]\n    result = near_term.compute_near_term(forecast([0, 0], [20, 20]), alerts, NT_CFG)\n    assert result[\"families\"][\"winter\"][\"score\"] == 80\n    assert result[\"families\"][\"hurricane\"][\"score\"] == 50\n    assert result[\"band\"] == \"Severe\"\n    assert any(\"Air Quality Alert\" in note for note in result[\"unmapped_alerts\"])\n\n\ndef test_band_boundaries():\n    bands = NT_CFG[\"bands\"]\n    assert near_term.band_for(24.9, bands) == \"Low\"\n    assert near_term.band_for(25, bands) == \"Guarded\"\n    assert near_term.band_for(75, bands) == \"Severe\"\n\n\n# -- ranking robustness -------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef test_rank_stability_detects_fragile_first_place():\n    # Two families with one lens each. A: x=80, y=40 → 60. B: x=40, y=78 → 59.\n    # x weight ×1.25: A 62.2 / B 56.9 (A first)   x ×0.75: A 57.1 / B 61.7 (B first)\n    # y weight ×1.25: A 57.8 / B 61.1 (B first)   y ×0.75: A 62.9 / B 56.3 (A first)\n    # 3 lens-weight scenarios ×2 cannot change anything (one lens per family) → 10 scenarios, top-1 holds in 8.\n    def bd(x, y):\n        lens = lambda s: {\"score\": s, \"lenses\": {\"modeled\": {\"score\": s}}, \"missing_lenses\": []}\n        return {\"families\": {\"x\": lens(x), \"y\": lens(y)}}\n\n    breakdowns = {\"A\": bd(80, 40), \"B\": bd(40, 78), \"C\": bd(10, 10)}\n    result = robustness.rank_stability(\n        breakdowns, families=[\"x\", \"y\"], family_weights={\"x\": 1, \"y\": 1},\n        lens_weights={\"observed\": 0.4, \"modeled\": 0.4, \"history\": 0.2}, perturbation=0.25, top_k=2,\n    )\n    assert result[\"scenarios\"] == 10\n    assert result[\"top1_unchanged\"] == 8\n    assert result[\"topk_unchanged\"] == 10  # {A, B} stays the top-2 set\n    assert result[\"baseline\"][:2] == [\"A\", \"B\"]\n\n\ndef test_ties_within_margin():\n    ranked = [(\"A\", 60.0), (\"B\", 58.5), (\"C\", 40.0)]\n    assert robustness.near_ties(ranked, margin=3.0, top_k=3) == [(\"A\", \"B\", 1.5)]\n"

{

  "content": "\"\"\"Small pure helpers shared by every score: normalization and threshold counting.\"\"\"\n\nimport bisect\nimport operator\nfrom collections.abc import Sequence\n\nfrom weather_risk.sources.open_meteo import DailyRow\n\nOPS = {\"ge\": operator.ge, \"gt\": operator.gt, \"le\": operator.le, \"lt\": operator.lt}\n\n\ndef piecewise(x: float, points: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Linear interpolation between (value, score) points sorted by value; flat outside the range.\"\"\"\n    xs = [p[0] for p in points]\n    if x <= xs[0]:\n        return float(points[0][1])\n    if x >= xs[-1]:\n        return float(points[-1][1])\n    i = bisect.bisect_right(xs, x)\n    (x0, y0), (x1, y1) = points[i - 1], points[i]\n    return y0 + (y1 - y0) * (x - x0) / (x1 - x0)\n\n\ndef anchor_score(value: float, full_score_at: float) -> float:\n    \"\"\"0 → 0, `full_score_at` → 100, capped (fixed anchors, not min-max — D11).\"\"\"\n    return piecewise(value, [[0, 0], [full_score_at, 100]])\n\n\ndef exceeds(value: float, op: str, threshold: float) -> bool:\n    return OPS[op](value, threshold)\n\n\ndef days_per_year(rows: list[DailyRow], variable: str, op: str, threshold: float) -> tuple[float | None, int]:\n    \"\"\"Mean qualifying days per year over days that have data. Returns (rate, n_valid_days).\"\"\"\n    values = [getattr(r, variable) for r in rows]\n    valid = [v for v in values if v is not None]\n    if not valid:\n        return None, 0\n    count = sum(1 for v in valid if exceeds(v, op, threshold))\n    return count * 365.25 / len(valid), len(valid)\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Deterministic \"% of days\" statistics over a date window.\"\"\"\n\nfrom datetime import date\n\nfrom weather_risk.scoring.indicators import exceeds\nfrom weather_risk.sources.open_meteo import DailyRow\n\n\ndef _count(values: list[float], op: str, threshold: float) -> int:\n    return sum(1 for v in values if exceeds(v, op, threshold))\n\n\ndef _pct(count: int, n: int) -> float | None:\n    return round(100.0 * count / n, 1) if n else None\n\n\ndef day_stat(rows: list[DailyRow], start: date, end: date, metric: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Count days meeting the metric's threshold in [start, end], plus a threshold-sensitivity table.\"\"\"\n    in_window = [r for r in rows if start <= r.date <= end]\n    values = [v for r in in_window if (v := getattr(r, metric[\"variable\"])) is not None]\n    days_in_window = (end - start).days + 1\n    count = _count(values, metric[\"op\"], metric[\"threshold\"])\n    return {\n        \"metric_label\": metric[\"label\"],\n        \"variable\": metric[\"variable\"],\n        \"op\": metric[\"op\"],\n        \"threshold\": metric[\"threshold\"],\n        \"count\": count,\n        \"days_with_data\": len(values),\n        \"days_in_window\": days_in_window,\n        \"pct\": _pct(count, len(values)),\n        \"coverage_pct\": round(100.0 * len(values) / days_in_window, 1),\n        \"sensitivity\": [\n            {\"label\": s[\"label\"], \"count\": (c := _count(values, s[\"op\"], s[\"threshold\"])), \"pct\": _pct(c, len(values))}\n            for s in metric.get(\"sensitivity\", [])\n        ],\n    }\n"
}

All date math lives here, never in the LLM.\"\"\"\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom datetime import date, timedelta\n\n\nclass WindowError(ValueError):\n    pass\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Window:\n    start: date\n    end: date\n    label: str\n    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\ndef _feb_end(year: int) -> date:\n    return date(year, 3, 1) - timedelta(days=1)\n\n\ndef resolve_window(\n    preset: str,\n    *,\n    today: date,\n    data_end: date,\n    data_start: date | None = None,\n    year: int | None = None,\n    start: date | None = None,\n    end: date | None = None,\n) -> Window:\n    notes: list[str] = []\n    match preset:\n        case \"last_calendar_year\":\n            y = today.year - 1\n            w_start, w_end, label = date(y, 1, 1), date(y, 12, 31), f\"calendar year {y}\"\n        case \"specific_year\":\n            if year is None:\n                raise WindowError(\"specific_year needs a year\")\n            w_start, w_end, label = date(year, 1, 1), date(year, 12, 31), f\"calendar year {year}\"\n        case \"year_to_date\":\n            w_start, w_end, label = date(today.year, 1, 1), data_end, f\"{today.year} year to date\"\n        case \"trailing_12_months\":\n            w_start, w_end, label = data_end - timedelta(days=364), data_end, \"trailing 12 months\"\n        case \"last_winter\":\n            # most recent fully completed Dec–Feb season\n            end_year = today.year if today.month >= 3 else today.year - 1\n            w_start, w_end = date(end_year - 1, 12, 1), _feb_end(end_year)\n            label = f\"winter {end_year - 1}–{str(end_year)[2:]} (Dec–Feb)\"\n        case \"custom\":\n            if start is None or end is None:\n                raise WindowError(\"custom window needs start_date and end_date\")\n            if start > end:\n                raise WindowError(f\"start {start} is after end {end}\")\n            w_start, w_end, label = start, end, f\"{start} to {end}\"\n        case _:\n            raise WindowError(f\"unknown time preset {preset!r}\")\n\n    if w_start > data_end:\n        raise WindowError(f\"no observed data after {data_end} (the archive lags ~6 days; forecasts are not observations)\")\n    if data_start and w_start < data_start:\n        raise WindowError(f\"stored daily data starts on {data_start.isoformat()}\")\n    if w_end > data_end:\n        notes.append(f\"Window clipped to {data_end} — the reanalysis archive lags real time by about 6 days.\")\n        w_end = data_end\n    return Window(w_start, w_end, label, notes)\n"

types = spec[\"incident_types\"]\n    matching = [\n        d for d in declarations\n        if d[\"incident_type\"] in types and date.fromisoformat(str(d[\"declaration_date\"])[:10]) >= since\n    ]\n    count = len(matching)\n    indicator = {\n        \"id\": \"fema_major_disasters\",\n        \"label\": f\"FEMA major-disaster declarations since {since.year} ({', '.join(types)})\",\n score_family(fam_cfg: dict, inputs: HubInputs, cfg: dict) -> dict:\n    lens_weights = cfg[\"lens_weights\"]\n    built = {\n        \"observed\": _observed_lens(fam_cfg.get(\"observed\") or [], inputs.declarations, cfg[\"declarations_since\"]),\n    }\n    lenses = {name: lens | {\"weight\": lens_weights[name]} for name, lens in built.items() if lens is not None}\n    missing = [name for   "content": "\"\"\"How far to trust a ranking: one-at-a-time weight perturbations and near-ties.\"\"\"\n\nfrom weather_risk.scoring.exposure import family_score_from_lenses\n\n\ndef _scores(breakdowns: dict[str, dict], families: list[str], family_weights: dict[str, float],\n            lens_weights: dict[str, float]) -> dict[str, float]:\n    out = {}\n    for hub, bd in breakdowns.items():\n        pairs = []\n        for f in families:\n            s = family_score_from_lenses(bd[\"families\"][f][\"lenses\"], lens_weights)\n            if s is not None:\n                pairs.append((family_weights.get(f, 0.0), s))\n        total = sum(w for w, _ in pairs)\n        if total > 0:\n            out[hub] = sum(w * s for w, s in pairs) / total\n    return out\n\n\ndef ranked(scores: dict[str, float]) -> list[str]:\n    return sorted(scores, key=lambda h: (-scores[h], h))\n\n\ndef rank_stability(\n    breakdowns: dict[str, dict],\n    *,\n    families: list[str],\n    family_weights: dict[str, float],\n    lens_weights: dict[str, float],\n    perturbation: float,\n    top_k: int,\n) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Re-rank with each family weight and each lens weight moved ±perturbation, one at a time.\"\"\"\n    baseline = ranked(_scores(breakdowns, families, family_weights, lens_weights))\n    scenarios: list[tuple[str, dict, dict]] = []\n    for factor, sign in ((1 + perturbation, \"+\"), (1 - perturbation, \"−\")):\n        for f in families:\n            scenarios.append((f\"{f} weight {sign}{perturbation:.0%}\", family_weights | {f: family_weights.get(f, 0.0) * factor}, lens_weights))\n        for lens in lens_weights:\n            scenarios.append((f\"{lens} lens weight {sign}{perturbation:.0%}\", family_weights, lens_weights | {lens: lens_weights[lens] * factor}))\n\n    top1_same = topk_same = 0\n    flips = []\n    for description, fw, lw in scenarios:\n        order = ranked(_scores(breakdowns, families, fw, lw))\n        if order[:1] == baseline[:1]:\n            top1_same += 1\n        elif len(flips) < 3:\n            flips.append(f\"{description}: {order[0]} ranks first\")\n        if set(order[:top_k]) == set(baseline[:top_k]):\n            topk_same += 1\n    return {\n        \"scenarios\": len(scenarios),\n        \"top1_unchanged\": top1_same,\n        \"topk_unchanged\": topk_same,\n        \"top_k\": top_k,\n        \"baseline\": baseline,\n        \"flips\": flips,\n    }\n\n\ndef near_ties(ranked_scores: list[tuple[str, float]], margin: float, top_k: int) -> list[tuple[str, str, float]]:\n    \"\"\"Adjacent pairs, down to the top-k boundary, whose scores are closer than `margin` points.\"\"\"\n    ties = []\n    for i in range(min(top_k, len(ranked_scores) - 1)):\n        (a, sa), (b, sb) = ranked_scores[i], ranked_scores[i + 1]\n        if sa - sb < margin:\n            ties.append((a, b, round(sa - sb, 1)))\n    return ties\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Numeric grounding: every number the explainer writes must come from the computed result.\n\nA number written with d decimals matches a source number if it equals that number\nrounded to d decimals (tolerance 0.5·10^-d). Small counting numbers (0-10) are always allowed.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nfrom typing import Any\n\n_NUMBER = re.compile(r\"(?<![\\w.])-?\\d{1,3}(?:,\\d{3})+(?:\\.\\d+)?|(?<![\\w.])-?\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?\")\n\n\ndef _normalize(text: str) -> str:\n    return text.replace(\"−\", \"-\").replace(\"–\", \" \").replace(\"—\", \" \")\n\n\ndef _tokens(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    return _NUMBER.findall(_normalize(text))\n\n\ndef extract_numbers(text: str) -> list[float]:\n    return [float(t.replace(\",\", \"\")) for t in _tokens(text)]\n\n\ndef allowed_numbers(bundle: Any, question: str = \"\") -> set[float]:\n    \"\"\"Every numeric value in the result (including numbers inside strings) plus the question.\"\"\"\n    found: set[float] = set(extract_numbers(question))\n\n    def walk(node: Any) -> None:\n        if isinstance(node, bool):\n            return\n        if isinstance(node, int | float):\n            found.add(float(node))\n        elif isinstance(node, str):\n            found.update(extract_numbers(node))\n        elif isinstance(node, dict):\n            for key, value in node.items():\n                walk(key)\n                walk(value)\n        elif isinstance(node, list | tuple):\n            for value in node:\n                walk(value)\n\n    walk(bundle)\n    return found\n\n\ndef ungrounded_numbers(text: str, allowed: set[float]) -> list[float]:\n    bad = []\n    for token in _tokens(text):\n        value = float(token.replace(\",\", \"\"))\n        if value.is_integer() and 0 <= value <= 10:\n            continue\n        decimals = len(token.split(\".\")[1]) if \".\" in token else 0\n        tolerance = 0.5 * 10**-decimals + 1e-9\n        if not any(abs(value - a) <= tolerance or abs(value + a) <= tolerance and value < 0 for a in allowed):\n            bad.append(value)\n    return bad\n"

any provider failure → next model\n            meta.provider_errors.append(f\"{model}: {exc.__class__.__name__}: {str(exc)[:200]}\")\n            continue\n        meta.model, meta.fallback_used = model, i > 0\n        return content\n    raise LLMUnavailableError(\"All LLM providers failed: \" + \" | \".join(meta.provider_errors))\n\n\nasync def structured_call(\n    messages: list[dict],\n    model_cls: type[T],\n    *,\n    models: list[str],\n    check: Callable[[T], None] | None = None,\n    completion: Callable[..., Awaitable[Any]] | None = None,\n    temperature: float = 0.0,\n    timeout: float = 30.0,\n) -> tuple[T, CallMeta]:\n    if completion is None:\n        import litellm\n\n        completion = litellm.acompletion\n    response_format = {\n        \"type\": \"json_schema\",\n        \"json_schema\": {\"name\": model_cls.__name__, \"strict\": True, \"schema\": strict_json_schema(model_cls)},\n    }\n    meta = CallMeta()\n    started = time.perf_counter()\n    msgs = list(messages)\n    try:\n        for attempt in (1, 2):\n            meta.attempts = attempt\n            content = await _complete(completion, msgs, models, response_format, meta, temperature, timeout)\n            try:\n                obj = model_cls.model_validate_json(content)\n                if check:\n                    check(obj)\n                return obj, meta\n            except ValueError as exc:  # \".join(f\"{key} = {m['label']}\" for key, m in cfg[\"stats\"].items()),\n    )\n    messages = [{\"role\": \"system\", \"content\": system}]\n    for turn in history:  # earlier turns: the question and the plan we resolved it to\n        messages.append({\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": turn[\"user_text\"]})\n        if turn.get(\"plan\"):\n            messages.append({\"role\": \"assistant\", \"content\": json.dumps(_compact(turn[\"plan\"]))})\n    messages.append({\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": question})\n    return messages\n\n\nasync def plan_question(question: str, history: list[dict], *, settings: Settings, today: date, data_start: date,\n                        data_end: date, completion=None) -> tuple[QueryPlan, CallMeta]:\n    messages = build_messages(question, history, today=today, data_start=data_start, data_end=data_end)\n    return await structured_call(messages, QueryPlan, models=[settings.llm_model, settings.llm_fallback_model],\n                                 completion=completion, temperature=0.0, timeout=settings.llm_timeout_s)\n"

  "content": "\"\"\"ResultBundle → Explanation. The LLM narrates; the grounding check keeps its numbers honest.\n\nIf the LLM is unavailable or still ungrounded after one retry, a deterministic template\nbuilt from the bundle is used instead — the answer never depends on the LLM being up.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom weather_risk.agent.executor import ResultBundle\nfrom weather_risk.agent.grounding import allowed_numbers, ungrounded_numbers\nfrom weather_risk.agent.llm import CallMeta, LLMError, structured_call\nfrom weather_risk.agent.schemas import Explanation\nfrom weather_risk.settings import Settings\n\nPROMPT = (Path(__file__).parent / \"prompts\" / \"explainer.md\").read_text()\n\n\ndef build_messages(question: str, bundle: ResultBundle) -> list[dict]:\n    result = json.dumps(bundle.for_llm(), ensure_ascii=False, default=str)\n    return [\n        {\"role\": \"system\", \"content\": PROMPT},\n        {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": f\"QUESTION: {question}\\n\\nRESULT:\\n{result}\"},\n    ]\n\n\ndef template_explanation(bundle: ResultBundle) -> Explanation:\n    return Explanation(\n        summary=bundle.headline,\n        reasoning=(bundle.points or [bundle.headline])[:5],\n        suggested_follow_ups=bundle.follow_ups[:3],\n    )\n\n\nasync def explain(question: str, bundle: ResultBundle, settings: Settings,\n                  completion=None) -> tuple[Explanation, CallMeta | None, str]:\n    \"\"\"Returns (explanation, call metadata, \"llm\" | \"template\").\"\"\"\n    allowed = allowed_numbers(bundle.for_llm(), question)\n\n    def check(explanation: Explanation) -> None:\n        bad = ungrounded_numbers(\" \".join([explanation.summary, *explanation.reasoning]), allowed)\n        if bad:\n            listed = \", \".join(f\"{b:g}\" for b in bad)\n            raise ValueError(f\"These numbers are not in RESULT: {listed}. Use only numbers that appear in RESULT.\")\n\n    try:\n        explanation, meta = await structured_call(\n            build_messages(question, bundle), Explanation,\n            models=[settings.llm_model, settings.llm_fallback_model],\n            check=check, completion=completion, temperature=0.2, timeout=settings.llm_timeout_s,\n        )\n        return explanation, meta, \"llm\"\n    except LLMError as exc:\n        return template_explanation(bundle), exc.meta, \"template\"\n"
}

\"\n                           f\"using data retrieved {success}.\")]\n    return []\n\n\ndef assemble(plan: QueryPlan, bundle: ResultBundle, explanation: Explanation, statuses: dict[str, dict],\n             meta: dict[str, Any], conversation_id: str | None = None) -> AgentAnswer:\n    reasons = list(bundle.uncertainty) + [(\"medium\", gap) for gap in bundle.data_gaps]\n    sources = []\n    for key in bundle.sources:\n        status = statuses.get(key, {})\n        reasons += _source_reasons(key, status)\n        name, url, detail = SOURCES[key]\n        sources.append(Source(name=name, url=url, retrieved_at=status.get(\"last_success_at\"), detail=detail))\n    if not reasons:\n        reasons = [(\"low\", \"Nothing was computed for this question.\" if not bundle.sources\n                    else \"All sources loaded and no data gaps were found.\")]\n    reasons.sort(key=lambda r: -SEVERITY[r[0]])\n    assumptions = list(dict.fromkeys([*bundle.assumptions, *plan.interpretation_notes]))\n    return AgentAnswer(\n        conversation_id=conversation_id,\n        intent=bundle.intent,\n        answer=explanation.summary,\n        reasoning=explanation.reasoning,\n        suggested_follow_ups=explanation.suggested_follow_ups,\n        table=bundle.rows,\n        breakdown=bundle.details or None,\n        assumptions=assumptions,\n        uncertainty=Uncertainty(level=reasons[0][0], reasons=list(dict.fromkeys(r for _, r in reasons))),\n        sources=sources,\n        time_windows=[TimeWindow(**w) for w in bundle.windows],\n        query_plan=plan.model_dump(mode=\"json\"),\n        meta=meta,\n    )\n\n\ndef error_answer(reason: str, conversation_id: str | None, meta: dict[str, Any]) -> AgentAnswer:\n    return AgentAnswer(\n        conversation_id=conversation_id,\n        intent=\"error\",\n        answer=\"I couldn't turn that question into a query I can compute. Please rephrase it — for example, \"\n               \"name the hubs, the hazard and the time frame.\",\n        reasoning=[reason],\n        suggested_follow_ups=[\"Which hubs in the Midwest are most exposed to winter disruption?\",\n                              \"What percentage of days in Denver last year had snowfall?\"],\n        table=[], breakdown=None, assumptions=[],\n        uncertainty=Uncertainty(level=\"high\", reasons=[reason]),\n        sources=[], time_windows=[], query_plan=None, meta=meta,\n    )\n\n\ndef render_markdown(answer: AgentAnswer) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Plain-text rendering for the CLI and eval reports.\"\"\"\n    lines = [answer.answer, \"\"]\n    lines += [f\"- {r}\" for r in answer.reasoning]\n    if answer.table:\n        cols = list(answer.table[0])\n        lines += [\"\", \"| \" + \" | \".join(cols) + \" |\", \"|\" + \"---|\" * len(cols)]\n        lines += [\"| \" + \" | \".join(str(row.get(c, \"\")) for c in cols) + \" |\" for row in answer.table]\n    lines += [\"\", f\"Uncertainty: {answer.uncertainty.level}\"] + [f\"  - {r}\" for r in answer.uncertainty.reasons]\n    lines += [\"Assumptions:\"] + [f\"  - {a}\" for a in answer.assumptions]\n    lines += [\"Time windows:\"] + [f\"  - {w.label}: {w.start or ''} → {w.end or ''}\" for w in answer.time_windows]\n    lines += [\"Sources:\"] + [f\"  - {s.name} (retrieved {s.retrieved_at})\" for s in answer.sources]\n    return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n"
}

  - Indicators are scored on fixed anchors from config/scoring.yaml (e.g. 25 snow days a year = 100), so scores do not depend on which other hubs are listed.
  - Overall exposure is the equal-weight average of 5 hazard families (winter, hurricane, flood, severe storm, heat).
Time windows:
  - Observed weather climatology (Open-Meteo ERA5): 2016-01-01 → 2025-12-31
  - FEMA National Risk Index (December 2025 release):  → 
  - FEMA major-disaster declarations: 2000-01-01 → 2026-10-01
Sources:
  - Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (ERA5 reanalysis) (retrieved 2026-10-01T14:48:50+00:00)
  - FEMA National Risk Index (county) (retrieved 2026-10-01T14:48:50+00:00)
  - OpenFEMA Disaster Declarations Summaries (retrieved 2026-10-01T14:48:50+00:00)

A missing role means analyst.\"\"\"\n    allowed: dict[str, Role] = {}\n    for item in filter(None, (part.strip() for part in raw.split(\",\"))):\n        email, _, role = item.partition(\":\")\n        role = role.strip().lower() or \"analyst\"\n        if role not in (\"analyst\", \"admin\"):\n            raise ValueError(f\"unknown role {role!r} for {email}\")\n        allowed[email.strip().lower()] = role  # type: ignore[assignment]\n    return allowed\n\n\ndef issue_token(user: User, settings: Settings) -> str:\n    now = datetime.now(UTC)\n    claims = {\"sub\": user.email, \"role\": user.role, \"iat\": now, \"exp\": now + timedelta(hours=settings.token_ttl_hours)}\n    return jwt.encode(claims, settings.jwt_secret, algorithm=\"HS256\")\n\n\ndef login(email: str, settings: Settings) -> tuple[User, str]:\n    role = parse_allowlist(settings.auth_allowlist).get(email.strip().lower())\n    if role is None:\n        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN, \"This email is not on the allow-list.\")\n    user = User(email=email.strip().lower(), role=role)\n    return user, issue_token(user, settings)\n\n\ndef current_user(request: Request, creds: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None = Depends(_bearer)) -> User:\n    if creds is None:\n        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, \"Missing bearer token — log in first.\")\n    settings: Settings = request.app.state.settings\n    try:\n        claims = jwt.decode(creds.credentials, settings.jwt_secret, algorithms=[\"HS256\"])\n    except jwt.PyJWTError as exc:\n        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, f\"Invalid token: {exc}\") from exc\n    # Re-check the allow-list so removing an email revokes access immediately.\n    role = parse_allowlist(settings.auth_allowlist).get(claims[\"sub\"])\n    if role is None:\n        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, \"This email is no longer on the allow-list.\")\n    return User(email=claims[\"sub\"], role=role)\n\n\ndef require_admin(user: User = Depends(current_user)) -> User:\n    if user.role != \"admin\":\n        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN, \"Admin role required.\")\n    return user\n"

# Built-in browser

The built-in browser is a real browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the person's Chrome. Its tools are named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` when the session itself runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when the session runs in the cloud (started from the web, a phone, or the desktop app) and is linked to the person's computer. The names after the prefix are the same either way, Claude uses whichever prefix is actually present, and this skill refers to the tools by the part after the prefix.

If the only built-in browser tool present is `enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser`, Claude calls it first: it turns the built-in browser on for this conversation, and the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` tools appear once it has run.

## What the person can see

The browser pane shares the desktop app's side panel with artifacts, documents, and file previews, and the panel shows one of them at a time. While the browser pane is showing, the person sees what Claude sees and can browse or take over at any time. While something else is open in the panel, or the panel is closed, the built-in browser keeps working but the person cannot see it.

Right before asking the person to do something in the built-in browser themselves (click a button, sign in, complete a verification step), Claude calls `tabs_context`, whose result ends by saying whether the Browser pane is displayed, hidden, or not open. If the pane is not open, Claude opens the page first and checks again. If the pane is hidden, Claude first asks the person to bring the browser back in the Claude desktop app: press Cmd+Shift+B on Mac or Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows, or close whatever else is open in the side panel and click the globe icon (the Browser button). Claude then says what to do in the browser. Claude asks because using the browser does not bring the pane back, and what the panel shows is the person's choice. Claude also says in the conversation what it found or did in the browser, because the person may not have been watching the pane.

## Sign-ins persist, and they are the person's

The built-in browser keeps its own persistent profile, shared across the desktop app's sessions. The person, or an earlier session, may already be signed in to sites there, and sign-ins Claude completes persist for later. Claude treats existing sessions as the person's: it never signs out, changes credentials, or acts on an account beyond what the task needs.

## Tabs

The built-in browser has tabs. `preview_start` with a `url` opens an additional tab at that URL in one call and returns a `tabId`, leaving existing tabs untouched, so Claude prefers it over `tabs_create` followed by `navigate` when the destination is already known. `navigate`, `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `computer`, `form_input`, and the console and network readers act on the tab named by `tabId`; omitting `tabId` targets the active tab, and `tabs_context` lists the open tabs.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Claude loads the built-in browser tools in bulk, not one-by-one: if they are in the deferred list, Claude loads them all in a single ToolSearch call whose query is their full name prefix, for example `{ query: "mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__", max_results: 64 }`.

## Reading pages

Claude prefers `get_page_text` and `read_page` over screenshots for reading, because they return the page's actual text and structure rather than pixels of the visible viewport. `computer` with action "screenshot" is for when the visual layout is the point or the person asks to see the page.

## Site approvals, blocked sites, and request_access

Depending on the person's approval settings, the person may be asked to approve a site before Claude acts on it, and some sites are blocked outright. Claude waits for a pending approval rather than working around it. If a page is refused or an approval is declined, Claude tells the person and moves on rather than retrying.

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, approvals can be answered from any of the person's devices and may take a moment to arrive, and the session may also have a `request_access` tool. If a browser tool answers that the site is not allowed yet and `request_access` is present, Claude calls it with that site's URL and scope "once" (or "site" when the task will keep using that site), waits for the person's answer, and then retries the original tool. Without `request_access`, a refused site is handled as above: Claude tells the person and moves on.

## What the built-in browser cannot open

The built-in browser cannot open `file://` URLs or `localhost` servers that Claude starts itself, because those run where Claude's shell runs, which is not where the browser pane runs. To show the person HTML that Claude generated, Claude uses an artifact instead.

## When the built-in browser cannot be reached

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, the pane runs in the Claude desktop app on the person's computer while Claude runs elsewhere, so it is reachable only while that app is open and online. If those tool calls cannot reach the desktop app (connection errors or no response), Claude tells the person the built-in browser looks offline on their computer rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

Before continuing M2, adjust M1 to match the narrow one-day scope we agreed on:

* Reduce the hub catalog to 8–10 representative hubs.
* Keep `config/hubs.yaml` and `config/scoring.yaml`; validate both at startup with typed models.
* Do not preload or record 10+ years of weather history.
* Use the previous 5 completed calendar years for default exposure analysis.
* Fetch historical Open-Meteo ERA5 data on demand with caching.
* Remove NWS forecast/alert ingestion and near-term scoring from the core implementation.
* Remove OpenFEMA disaster declaration ingestion from the core implementation.
* Keep the core public data sources to:
   * Open-Meteo historical ERA5 daily weather
   * FEMA National Risk Index county hazard data
* Recorded real API responses are useful as deterministic test fixtures, but seed ingestion must not be a runtime dependency.
* Keep bonus alerting and voice outside the core path until the agent, API, UI, and evals work.
* Before changing an already agreed technology choice, call it out first and explain why.
* Re-check persistence against the agreed async SQLAlchemy + SQLite approach. If you believe stdlib `sqlite3` is materially better for this assignment, explain the trade-off before continuing.

Preserve the useful work already completed:

* verified FIPS values
* YAML configuration structure
* recorded real API fixtures
* applicable source adapters/tests
* TDD approach

Also preserve these UI decisions for the later Streamlit milestone:

* Global navigation is at the top, not in a global sidebar.
* Main pages:
   * `Home`
   * `Chat`
   * `Analytics`
* `Home` is a concise welcome/explanation page with methodology, data sources, limitations, and example questions.
* `Chat` has a sidebar only for conversation history:
   * New Chat
   * previous conversations
   * reopen and continue an existing conversation
* Voice input must be integrated directly into/beside the chat input, not on a separate page.
* `Analytics` visualizes the same deterministic results used by chat: rankings, hub comparisons, hazard-family scores, and historical exposure metrics.
* Alert settings should eventually allow:
   * generic webhook URL
   * enabled/disabled
   * score-change threshold
   * Test Webhook
* Webhooks must remain provider-agnostic; Make is only one possible consumer.

self.window[0][0] >= 60:\n                    self.window.popleft()\n                used = sum(w for _, w in self.window)\n                if not self.window or used + weight <= self.per_minute:\n                    self.window.append((now, weight))\n                    return\n                await self.sleep(60 - (now - self.window[0][0]))\n\n\nclass WeatherService:\n    STALE_AFTER = timedelta(hours=12)\n\n    def __init__(self, db: Database, client: httpx.AsyncClient, limiter: RateLimiter, *,\n                 today_fn: Callable[[], date] = date.today, now_fn: Callable[[], datetime] = utcnow):\n        self.db, self.client, self.limiter = db, client, limiter\n        self.today_fn, self.now_fn = today_fn, now_fn\n        self._locks: dict[tuple[str, int], asyncio.Lock] = {}\n\n    def _needs_fetch(self, entry, complete: bool) -> bool:\n        if entry is None:\n            return True\n        if entry.complete:\n            return False\n        fetched = entry.fetched_at if entry.fetched_at.tzinfo else entry.fetched_at.replace(tzinfo=UTC)\n        return complete or self.now_fn() - fetched > self.STALE_AFTER\n\n    async def _ensure_year(self, hub: Hub, year: int) -> str | None:\n        today = self.today_fn()\n        start, end, complete = year_span(year, today)\n        if start > end:\n            return None\n        async with self._locks.setdefault((hub.id, year), asyncio.Lock()):\n            entry = (await self.db.fetch_log(hub.id)).get(year)\n            if not self._needs_fetch(entry, complete):\n                return None\n            await self.limiter.acquire(open_meteo.call_weight((end - start).days + 1))\n            try:\n                payload = await open_meteo.fetch_archive(self.client, hub.lat, hub.lon, start, end)\n                rows = open_meteo.parse_daily(payload)\n            except (SourceError, ValueError, KeyError) as exc:\n                await self.db.source_error(\"open_meteo_archive\", str(exc))\n                cached = \" — using the copy cached earlier\" if entry else \"\"\n                return f\"{hub.name} {year}: Open-Meteo request failed ({exc}){cached}.\"\n            await self.db.upsert_daily(hub.id, rows)\n            await self.db.record_fetch(hub.id, year, complete=complete, grid=open_meteo.grid_cell(payload))\n            await self.db.source_ok(\"open_meteo_archive\")\n            return None\n\n    async def ensure(self, hub: Hub, start: date, end: date) -> list[str]:\n        \"\"\"Make sure [start, end] is cached. datetime.fromisoformat(cached[0])\n                if age < self.TTL and needed <= set(cached[1][\"by_fips\"]):\n                    return cached[1], []\n            try:\n                pages = await nri.fetch_county_pages(self.client)\n                version, n, by_fips = nri.county_percentiles(pages, sorted(needed))\n            except (SourceError, ValueError, KeyError) as exc:\n                await self.db.source_error(\"fema_nri\", str(exc))\n                if cached:\n                    return cached[1], [f\"FEMA National Risk Index refresh failed ({exc}); \"\n                                       f\"using data retrieved {cached[0]}.\"]\n                return None, [f\"FEMA National Risk Index unavailable ({exc}) — modeled-loss evidence is missing.\"]\n            payload = {\n                \"version\": version,\n                \"n_counties\": n,\n                \"by_fips\": {f: {hz: {\"alrb\": v.alrb, \"pct\": v.pct} for hz, v in m.items()} for f, m in by_fips.items()},\n            }\n            await self.db.cache_put(\"nri\", \"fema_nri\", payload)\n            await self.db.source_ok(\"fema_nri\")\n            return payload, []\n"

  "content": "\"\"\"Long-term Exposure Score (for investment decisions) — docs/DECISIONS.md D10–D12, D20.\n\nfamily score = weighted mean of its evidence lenses (observed weather, modeled NRI loss),\n               renormalized over the lenses that exist by design or loaded successfully;\noverall      = weighted mean of family scores (equal weights by default).\nEvery intermediate value is kept in the returned breakdown so \"why\" answers can cite it.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom statistics import mean\n\nfrom weather_risk.config import Family, ScoringConfig\nfrom weather_risk.scoring.indicators import anchor_score, days_per_year\nfrom weather_risk.sources.open_meteo import DailyRow\n\nLENS_SOURCES = {\n    \"observed\": \"Open-Meteo archive (ERA5 reanalysis)\",\n    \"modeled\": \"FEMA National Risk Index\",\n}\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass HubInputs:\n    daily: list[DailyRow]  # empty = no weather data available\n    nri: dict[str, dict] | None  # hazard code → {\"alrb\", \"pct\"}; None = source unavailable\n\n\ndef _observed_lens(family: Family, daily: list[DailyRow]) -> dict | None:\n    if not family.observed:\n        return None  # lens not used for this family (by design)\n    indicators = []\n    for spec in family.observed:\n        rate, _ = days_per_year(daily, spec.variable, spec.op, spec.threshold)\n        if rate is None:\n            return {\"score\": None, \"indicators\": [], \"source\": LENS_SOURCES[\"observed\"]}\n        indicators.append({\"id\": spec.id, \"label\": spec.label, \"raw\": rate, \"unit\": \"days/yr\",\n                           \"full_score_at\": spec.full_score_at, \"score\": anchor_score(rate, spec.full_score_at)})\n    return {\"score\": mean(i[\"score\"] for i in indicators), \"indicators\": indicators, \"source\": LENS_SOURCES[\"observed\"]}\n\n\ndef _modeled_lens(family: Family, nri: dict[str, dict] | None, names: dict[str, str]) -> dict | None:\n    if family.modeled is None:\n        return None\n    indicators = [\n        {\"id\": f\"nri_{code}\", \"label\": f\"{names[code]}: building loss rate, national percentile\",\n         \"raw\": nri[code][\"pct\"], \"unit\": \"percentile\", \"applicable\": nri[code][\"alrb\"] is not None,\n         \"score\": nri[code][\"pct\"]}\n        for code in family.modeled.nri\n        if nri and code in nri\n    ]\n    if not indicators:\n        return {\"score\": None, \"indicators\": [], \"source\": LENS_SOURCES[\"modeled\"]}\n    combine = max if family.modeled.combine == \"max\" else mean\n    return {\"score\": combine(i[\"score\"] for i in indicators), \"combine\": family.modeled.combine,\n            \"indicators\": indicators, \"source\": LENS_SOURCES[\"modeled\"]}\n\n\ndef family_score_from_lenses(lenses: dict[str, dict], factors: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> float | None:\n    \"\"\"Weighted mean of available lens scores. `factors` scale lens weights (robustness checks).\"\"\"\n    factors = factors or {}\n    available = [(lens[\"weight\"] * factors.get(name, 1.0), lens[\"score\"])\n                 for name, lens in lenses.items() if lens.get(\"score\") is not None]\n    if not available or sum(w for w, _ in available) <= 0:\n        return None\n    return sum(w * s for w, s in available) / sum(w for w, _ in available)\n\n\ndef score_family(name: str, inputs: HubInputs, cfg: ScoringConfig) -> dict:\n    family = cfg.families[name]\n    weights = cfg.lens_weights_for(name)\n    built = {\n        \"observed\": _observed_lens(family, inputs.daily),\n        \"modeled\": _modeled_lens(family, inputs.nri, cfg.nri_hazard_names),\n    }\n    lenses = {lens: data | {\"weight\": getattr(weights, lens)} for lens, data in built.items() if data is not None}\n    missing = [lens for lens, data in lenses.items() if data[\"score\"] is None]\n    total_w = sum(data[\"weight\"] for data in lenses.values())\n    return {\n        \"label\": family.label,\n        \"score\": family_score_from_lenses(lenses),\n        \"lenses\": lenses,\n        \"missing_lenses\": missing,\n        \"missing_weight_share\": sum(lenses[m][\"weight\"] for m in missing) / total_w if total_w else 0.0,\n    }\n\n\ndef overall_score(breakdown: dict, family_weights: dict[str, float], families: list[str] | None = None) -> float | None:\n    \"\"\"Weighted mean of family scores; families without a score are skipped.\"\"\"\n    families = families or list(family_weights)\n    pairs = [(family_weights.get(f, 0.0), breakdown[\"families\"][f][\"score\"])\n             for f in families if breakdown[\"families\"].get(f, {}).get(\"score\") is not None]\n    total = sum(w for w, _ in pairs)\n    if not pairs or total <= 0:\n        return None\n    return sum(w * s for w, s in pairs) / total\n\n\ndef compute_exposure(hub_id: str, inputs: HubInputs, cfg: ScoringConfig,\n                     family_weights: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> dict:\n    weights = family_weights or cfg.family_weights\n    families = {name: score_family(name, inputs, cfg) for name in cfg.families}\n    breakdown = {\"hub_id\": hub_id, \"families\": families, \"family_weights\": weights}\n    breakdown[\"score\"] = overall_score(breakdown, weights)\n    scored = {f: v for f, v in families.items() if v[\"score\"] is not None}\n    total_w = sum(weights.get(f, 0.0) for f in scored)\n    for f, fam in families.items():\n        fam[\"contribution\"] = fam[\"score\"] * weights.get(f, 0.0) / total_w if f in scored and total_w else None\n    breakdown[\"top_family\"] = max(scored, key=lambda f: scored[f][\"score\"]) if scored else None\n    gaps = [f\"{LENS_SOURCES[lens]} unavailable — {fam['label']} score uses the remaining evidence.\"\n            for fam in families.values() for lens in fam[\"missing_lenses\"]]\n    breakdown[\"data_gaps\"] = list(dict.fromkeys(gaps))\n    return breakdown\n"

 def data_end(self) -> date:\n        return archive_end(self.today)\n\n    async def exposure(self, hub_ids: list[str] | None = None) -> Exposure:\n        \"\"\"Exposure breakdowns for the given 1	# Key decisions
2	
3	Each entry gives the decision, why it was made, and what was rejected. The evidence comes from live API calls made during planning (2026-10-01); see [PLAN.md §0](PLAN.md#0-data-sources--verified-with-live-read-only-calls-2026-10-01).
4	
5	| # | Decision | Area |
6	|---|---|---|
7	| D1 | The LLM plans and explains; code computes every number | Agent |
8	| D2 | Plan → execute → explain, not a free-form tool loop | Agent |
9	| D3 | Flat, strict JSON schemas + local validation + grounding check | Agent |
10	| D4 | Assumptions, uncertainty, sources and time window are generated by code | Agent |
11	| D5 | Groq `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, Gemini fallback, pinned LiteLLM | LLM |
12	| D6 | Four public sources, each with one job | Data |
13	| D7 | NRI building loss rate → our own national percentile | Data |
14	| D8 | FEMA: major disasters only, weather types only | Data |
15	| D9 | 10-year observation window (2016–2025) | Data |
16	| D10 | Two scores: long-term exposure and near-term risk | KPI |
17	| D11 | Fixed-anchor normalization, not min-max | KPI |
18	| D12 | Overall exposure = equal-weight mean of families | KPI |
19	| D13 | Stat thresholds in config, always printed | KPI |
20	| D14 | SQLite + committed seed snapshot | Storage |
21	| D15 | One run script; Docker optional; no cloud deploy yet | Ops |
22	| D16 | Eval: offline by default, `--live` for the real LLM | Eval |
23	| D17 | Pragmatic TDD for core logic | Process |
24	| D18 | Identity-lite auth | Security |
